evidence: Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “in the language of common life, in the tone of conversation”. With cum and the ablative, talk to or with someone; with dē, talk about. To speak in public, as an orator, is dīcere.

evidence: Cic. Att. 5.1.3: in prīmīs nōbīs sermō isque multus dē tē fuit
terms.comment: Sermōnem cum aliquō cōnferre or habēre, to have a talk with someone; also a language (see language).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.32: quod conloquimur inter nōs
Cic. Q. fr. 2.8.1: et obloquāre et colloquāre
terms.comment: With cum aliquō or inter sē; the noun is colloquium.

terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; posteā Suet., Gell.
evidence: Ter. Ph. 654: ut apertē tibi nunc fābuler
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “esp. freq. in Plaut.; not in Cic.”.

terms.gloss: speak; of a child, begin to talk
terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor.; dē puerīs prīmum loquentibus Varr., Gell., Suet.
evidence: Varr. LL 6.52: puerī dīcuntur īnfantēs; cum id faciunt, jam fārī
Suet. Aug. 94.7: cum prīmum fārī coepisset

terms.comment: Lewis & Short: early and colloquial for colloquor; with cum aliquō.

evidence: Plaut. Poen. prol. 34: dum sermōnēs fābulandī cōnferant (Lewis & Short s.v. sermō)

terms.comment: Lewis & Short: common talk, rumour; rare but classical.

phrases.english: Talking to you is like talking to myself.

phrases.latin: Hōc enim ūnō praestāmus vel maximē ferīs, quod conloquimur inter nōs
phrases.english: For in this one thing above all we surpass the beasts: that we talk with one another

phrases.latin: ībat rēx obsitus aevō et comitem Aenēān juxtā nātumque tenēbat ingrediēns variōque viam sermōne levābat
phrases.english: The old king walked along, keeping Aeneas and his son beside him, and lightened the road with talk of this and that.

phrases.latin: fīlius Croesī rēgis, cum jam fārī per aetātem posset, īnfāns erat
phrases.english: King Croesus’s son, when he was old enough to talk, still could not speak
to have a talk with someone
to talk something over with someone
